links.reason: Kural 617 (தாளுளான் தாமரையினாள்) ties Lakshmi to effort; the verse says only that she will not embrace வழுவினார். A slip is not sloth, and the verse is a blessing in a flagged line (புல்லாள்ட்), so 'condition' for the couplet is a generous reading.
links.text_issue: line 4 has a stray letter; lines 1-2 hard to construe

links.reason: Line 1 கறங்கென வினையினோடி puts deeds as the wheel's driver, and Kural 361 says அவா is the seed of birth; the contrast is real but each tradition names both elsewhere, so 'different roots' is thin and not a true qualification.

Verse 747 never names the Vidyadhara hill; it has bangled women and falling petals in groves, verse 126 has powder staining rocks. A generic pleasure-on-hill setting is a shared topic, not a distinctive image.
Kural 638 is about an unheeding king; 361 has counsellors urging haste (மந்திரம் நீளுமாயின்) and the verse does not say the king accepts. The pair gives no hard case/easy case, only counsel given.

455 has an unnamed hearer raging (வெகுண்டான்); 693 does not mention the cattle raid, only 'hearing what Civakan is'. Identifying the two as the same news and the same man is reconstructed from the plot, not the Tamil.
Kural 1067 says do not beg of those who conceal (கரப்பார்); Pazhamozhi 224 gives the reason in மரம்போல் வலிய மனத்தார் and the proverb பள்ளியுள் ஐயம் புகல். The image adds why such begging fails.
Kural 8 அறவாழி and 3023 அறவாழி with குணக்கடல் show the word read as wheel and sea, a real point, but it is a shared image, not a qualification, and the Kural gains no new 'use'.

Kural 543 makes the king's கோல் the source of dharma; verse 2746 assigns நூற்கடன் to the ascetic and கோற்கடன் to the king, which splits duties. It does not say the king comes to be taught or rank them, so 'disagree about authority' overreads it.
324 is the birds feeding after the elephant's rampage in 314 (விருந்தவையுண), so it is aftermath in story order. The 'cost seen in what scavengers gain' is not stated by either verse.
Kural 764 defines the army that does not collapse (அழிவின்றி); 1250 shows an army's drums and crowns overthrown. That is the couplet illustrated by its negative, with no limit or condition added.

Tivittan calls the demander a fool taking a jewel from a cobra's hood; Kural 894 is the weak harming the strong (கூற்றத்தைக் கையால் விளித்தல்). Same logic, different image; nothing is 'turned against' the demander as a qualification.

Kural 3 மலர்மிசை ஏகினான் and 2814 தாமரைமேற் சென்ற திருவாரடி share the lotus-walker, and the epic adds the five-six-nine categories. But the verse states no promise of long life, so the epic-side gain is untrue.

Line 4 புண்மேற் கிழிபோற் றுறத்தல் is the wives' complaint, reported and not endorsed; the epic itself praises his renunciation. Pairing it with Naladiyar 53 as a cost is fair, but the note's 'opposing view' gain is backwards and a tension is not stated.

549 praises a match of equal ஓங்கிய குலம் and செல்வம்; Naladiyar 195 says குலம் is only a word. The note itself concedes the clash holds only if lineage means inherited rank, and political matching is a different situation from defining worth.

Verse 86 shows the elephant tearing loose and killing the mahouts; nothing says it was loosed by anyone, and Naladiyar 213 is about friendship with elephant-like men. 'Weapon someone else loosed' is not in the Tamil.
1647 searches the grove (சோதித்து) and posts guards; 1630 has the hidden prince beside the women. The irony of guards missing him is plausible, but 'protects the game not the king' is not in 1647.

Naga 36 says those who bow to the non-killing lord reach release; TM 200 says those who give up killing, theft, lust and lying reach Siva's feet. Both pair non-killing with release, so there is no incompatible claim; the keeper-of-vow difference is an overreading.
1247 இருள்பாயின and மருள்வார் வெருள்வார் show confused flight in darkness; Kural 775 is about blinking at a thrown spear. No arrow-blinding is stated, so no case for 'is blinking cowardice' is made.
539 has the astrologer name Rajamapuram; 610 has the Hastinapuram king arrive. The fulfilment and 'journey in vain' rest on the later plot (who wins), not on the two verses.

1279 காலனையு நோனார் and அச்சமுடையார் அகல்க make the warriors screen the fearful out; Kural 765 கூற்றுடன்று...கூடி எதிர்நிற்கும் names fearlessness before Death as the army's essence. The selection scene extends it.

Kural 146 says the four ills never leave one who crosses into another's home; 214 only recalls the poisoning and the hunchback lover. No disease or fruit for the wife is stated, so the added 'bodily fruit' is not in the verse.

640 has kings vow war if another wins; 844 says a wicked one 'burning at heart' said she belongs to the strongest spear and began war. The threat and war do connect, but 'one instigator breaking the contest's law' is an interpretation of கொடியான்.
157 has the serpent as a simile for Saccandan's wrath; in 290 the serpent is the minister (மாநாகம்) swallowing him. Different bearers, so 'the same wrath turned back on him' is invented.

351 shows a youth turned from music and dance (வெறுத்து நின்றான்) but names no one and gives no old-age reason, and Naladiyar 11's argument is the grey hair. 'A named young man' is not in the verse; it is illustration.

1456 அதனையும் அறிந்து shows Tivittan answering the sleep arrow of 1455 (கண்களைத் துயிற்றும் அம்பு) with துயில்விடை செய்யும் அம்பு. The later unit reverses the earlier, which is a real within-epic link.

158 shows Prithivi Devi leaving her son (தன் பெருமகனை விட்டு) for austerity and reaching Achyuta; Kural 46's புறத்தாற்றில் போஒய்ப் பெறுவ தெவன் asks what leaving gains. The epic answers that question with the Jain reply, so tension fits.

775 praises giving oneself to end beings' pain (என்னைக் கொடுத்தும்); TM 724 keeps the body alive for knowledge. These do not conflict; one is an ethic of sacrifice, the other a yogic physiology. No incompatible claim.

3101 நின்...சேவடி...கருவினை துணிக்கு மெஃகமே names how the Lord's feet cut karma; Kural 5 says இருவினையும் சேரா to those who praise him. The cutting image supplies the means to the couplet's assurance.
Both show dogs tearing hell's victims (ஞமலி, செந்நாய்), a conventional Jain hell image. Only 1933 has the thorn tree and caged rearing, so 'dog and thorn tree recur' is false.

Naladiyar 51 says sin returns when the merit runs out; 3064 துணிய வீர்ந்திடும் துப்பமை சிந்தையான் cuts the eight karmas. Whether the cut is final is the epic's own context, not this verse, so the contrast is read in.
944 shows the dog's ears pricked and tears (செவி யோர்த்து...நீரொடு), set against Naladiyar 322's tanner's dog; the inversion is real. But 'broken at death' and 'consents' are not in the verse.
1336 is a vow (மண்ணகமு நமதாச் செய்வென்) and 1350 is a fall of an unnamed சுடர்வேலான்; the verses do not name Suvanakethu as the fallen. The fulfilment depends on a reconstructed plot.

Both put drying fish and prawns on the shore for neythal, but the two poems are different poems. Kuruntokai 320 says she has not even laughed with him (நக்கதோர் பழியும் இலமே) and Kainnilai 54 says he lied and enjoyed her (பொய்த்தெம்மை...நலனுண்ட): different women, not incompatible.

563 gives daughters as conch-pearls profiting others (மகளிர்); Naladiyar 274 uses a house daughter as a simile for a miser's wealth enjoyed by a stranger. The shared 'daughter goes to another' is thin and the father's felt loss is not in the verse.

292 has a warrior seizing his place at the toddy (என்முறை வருக என்னான்) and 298 has a warrior complaining the king does not say நீ முந்து. They are two poems on a similar theme, so neither develops the other.

334 has a speaker warning a hero of the girl's arms turning to enmity; the roll of princes it supposedly completes is not in this verse. Kural 504 asks to weigh qualities and faults; nothing in 334 enacts or fails that.

2587 recalls that the usurper threw her out of the stage and jailed her; 686 has his assault in an image. Whether they are the same event is not stated, and 'an injury against Civakan' is not in the Tamil.

1988 தேனெய் அழிதுளி நக்கும் with the pit, elephant and snake pictures the pleasure-in-danger that Naladiyar 60 describes (இன்பமே காமுறுவர் ஏழையார்). It extends rather than qualifies; the pair teaches a little.

262 sandal that keeps coolness under the rutting elephant and bearing lapses wins homage; Naladiyar 66 bears the base's words, held back by lineage. They agree; the reward-versus-reason difference is true but small.

2764 simply describes a hell of blades with no one named; Naladiyar-style jailers are absent from this verse only because it is a scene description. Reading silence as a rival theory of who runs hell is not in the Tamil.
1419 and 1420 are consecutive verses of one fight; the note adds a reversal of an 'earlier victory' and 'wins by fear' that neither verse states. Sequence, not a link.

2603 has Vijayai honour the one who rescued her in the சுடுகாடு; 302 has her grieving in the forest (காட்டுள்) without naming a burning ground or a rescuer. The callback is plausible; 'grief turned into a debt honoured' is interpretation.

39 puts stores in charge of those with no அறிவு to match their size, with the crow image (காக்கைக்குக் காப்படுத்த சோறு); Kural 507 is about trusting out of காதன்மை. The verse never mentions fondness, and the line 1-2 parse is uncertain.
Two infants named Vijayan are linked on the name alone (திருவொடு வென்றியிற் சேரு மாதலால் in 1722). A shared name is not an image, and 71 does not tie the two persons.
